correctness.rationale: The Alexander dual has all vertices and pairs, induced two-edge paths as 2-faces and four-cycles as 3-simplices; 5-faces are impossible by the 10 triple/3 edge incidence count. The K_(2,3)-free condition makes each non-square path diagonal free. Each square has a private graph edge, so one tetrahedron-triangle and three subsequent triangle-edge elementary collapses can be made without interference from adjacent square tetrahedra. The connected residual graph has C(N,2)-T+q edges, hence B independent loops. Alexander duality and simplex low-skeleton connectivity imply an integral wedge of spheres, not just a mod-two Betti count. Independently built adjacency, dual-faces and all freeness checks for Mobius ladders m=4..8, obtaining B=1,11,25,43,65; finite checks corroborate rather than prove unbounded m.

The published Mobius-ladder *total* three-cut uses independent triples, not disconnected triples, so its homotopy calculation is a different functor. Full Resultary earlier proofs and the original ordinary cut-complex framework were compared. value.rationale: A natural homotopy-type extension resolves overlapping four-cycle incidences in ordinary graph cut complexes; a uniform explicit collapse lemma and infinite Mobius-ladder family replace an edge-disjoint restriction. Integral top-dimensional sphere multiplicities are useful exact structural data, not a small arbitrary instance.

final_claim: For any finite triangle-free simple graph with N>=8, at most two common neighbors per vertex pair, and a private cycle edge on every four-cycle, ordinary Delta_3(G) is a wedge of B(G)=C(N-1,2)-sum_v C(d(v),2)+q(G) spheres S^(N-4); for Mobius ladder M_(2m), m>=4, B=2m^2-8m+1.
